learning.learning_goal: Compare two groups by pairing them, then name the difference and write a subtraction.
learning.big_idea: Pair one blue dot with one red dot. Count the blue dots left over to find how many more.
assumed_prior_knowledge: Count objects one by one up to 10 and know the last number said is the total.
Match one item from one group with one item from another group.

screens.label: Comparison 1
screens.title: How many more?
screens.body: Count two groups of dots. Then see how many more blue dots there are.

screens.label: Count
screens.title: How many blue dots?

visual.ariaLabel: Blue: dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot. Red: dot, dot, dot, dot.

choices.feedback: Four counts red. Count blue from the left.
Yes. You counted 6 blue dots.
Ten joins both rows. Count only blue.

hints: Touch each blue dot as you count.
Start at the left blue dot. Say one number for each dot.

screens.label: Count
screens.title: How many red dots?

visual.ariaLabel: Blue: dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot. Red: dot, dot, dot, dot.

choices.feedback: Six counts blue. Count only red.
Ten joins both rows. Count only red.
Yes. You counted 4 red dots.

hints: Touch each red dot as you count.
Start at the left red dot. Say one number for each dot.

screens.label: Watch
screens.title: Put one blue with one red.

visual.ariaLabel: Four outlined pairs, each with one blue dot above one red dot; two blue dots remain outside the outlines.
visual.message: Each outline holds one blue dot and one red dot.

screens.label: Discover
screens.title: How many blue dots are left?

visual.ariaLabel: Pair, pair, pair, pair; then blue dot, blue dot without red partners.
visual.message: Some blue dots are outside the pairs. Count them.

choices.feedback: Six counts every blue dot. Look after the pairs.
Yes. Two blue dots are left. There are 2 more blue dots than red dots.
Ten joins both colors. Count blue without partners.

hints: Look to the right of the four pairs.
Count the blue dots without a red dot below them.

screens.label: Language
screens.title: The difference is 2.

visual.ariaLabel: Four blue and red pairs, plus two extra blue dots.
visual.message: Two blue dots are left after pairing.

screens.guidance: “How many more?” and “What is the difference?” both ask for those 2 extra blue dots.

screens.label: Remember
screens.title: How many more? Find the difference.
screens.body: The difference is 2. Write it as 6 − 4 = 2. This is subtraction.

screens.label: Misconception
screens.title: Does “more” mean add here?
screens.prompt: Ava has 8 stickers. Luis has 5. How many more does Ava have?

choices.feedback: Thirteen joins both groups. Count Ava’s dots after the pairs.
Yes. Five stickers pair up. Three of Ava’s are left, so the difference is 3.
Eight is Ava’s whole group. Count her dots without partners.

hints: We want Ava’s extra stickers, not both groups together.
Match 5 of Ava’s stickers with Luis’s 5. How many of Ava’s are left?

visual.ariaLabel: Ava: dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot. Luis: dot, dot, dot, dot, dot. Five paired positions.
visual.message: One dot stands for one sticker. The outlines show pairs.

screens.label: Symbol
screens.title: Which subtraction matches the dots?

visual.ariaLabel: Four outlined blue and red pairs, then two extra blue dots.
visual.message: Six blue. Four have red partners.

choices.feedback: Yes. Six blue dots minus four paired dots leaves two. The difference is 2.
Adding joins the groups. We need extra blue dots.
Start with six blue, then subtract four paired blue dots.

hints: Start with all 6 blue dots. Four have a red partner.
Which choice starts at 6 and removes the 4 paired dots?

visual.ariaLabel: Four blue and red pairs, plus two extra blue dots.

screens.label: Guided practice
screens.title: How many more blue dots?

visual.message: Each outline shows one blue and one red dot. Which blue dots are left?
visual.ariaLabel: Pair, pair, pair, pair; then blue dot, blue dot, blue dot without red partners.

choices.feedback: Yes. Four pairs and three blue dots left over. There are 3 more blue dots.
Eleven joins the colors. Count only extra blue dots.
Four counts red. Count blue after the pairs.

hints: Find each outlined pair.
After the last pair, count the blue dots without red partners.

screens.label: Independent practice
screens.title: Try one without dots.
screens.prompt: Nia read 9 pages. Theo read 5 pages. How many more pages did Nia read?

choices.feedback: 9 − 5 = 4. Nia read 4 more pages.
Fourteen joins the pages. Find Nia’s extra pages.
Five is Theo’s count. Count from five to nine.

hints: Each dot below stands for one page. Find Nia’s dots without a partner.
Or count from 5 up to 9. How many steps?

supportVisual.ariaLabel: Nia: dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot. Theo: dot, dot, dot, dot, dot.
supportVisual.message: One dot stands for one page. Count Nia’s dots without a partner.

screens.label: Recall
screens.title: Another way to ask “how many more”?
screens.prompt: There are 6 blue dots and 4 red dots. Which question asks for the extra blue dots?

choices.feedback: “In all” joins the groups. Find the phrase for extras.
Yes. The difference is how many more blue dots there are: 6 − 4 = 2.
“How many blue?” counts all blue dots. Find the phrase for extras.

hints: “In all” asks you to join both groups.
Find the question that asks how many more blue dots there are.

screens.label: Transfer
screens.title: Try it with prices.
screens.prompt: One notebook costs $10. Another costs $8. What is the difference in price?

choices.feedback: $10 − $8 = $2. The difference is $2.
Eighteen adds both prices. Find how much higher ten is than eight.
Ten is one price, not the difference. Count from eight to ten.

hints: A difference in price tells how much more one costs.
Start at $8. Count up to $10. How much did you add?

screens.label: Reflect
screens.title: What does “difference” mean?
screens.prompt: When we compare 6 blue dots with 4 red dots, what is the difference?

choices.feedback: No dots are removed here. We compare the groups.
All together gives a total. Difference asks for the extras.

choices.text: How many more blue dots there are.
choices.feedback: The two extra blue dots show the difference.

hints: Pair one blue with one red.
What do the blue dots left over tell you?

screens.title: You found the difference.
screens.body: Count the extras to answer “how many more?” or “what is the difference?”
